newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Halliburton, British Cairn Energy sign deal.
newsitem.headline: Halliburton, British Cairn Energy sign deal.

text.p: Britain's Cairn Energy Plc and American Halliburton Co. signed a $235 million deal to develop natural gas fields in Bangladesh, government officials said.
Prime Minister Sheikhh Hasina, visiting British Prime Minister John Major and Halliburton chief Dick Cheney, the former U.S. defence secretary, witnessed the signing of the contract.
Cairn will invest $150 million to jointly develop the Sangu gas field in the Bay of Bengal with Halliburton spending $85 million.
The first gas is due to come on stream in 1998.
A U.S embassy statement on Saturday said the aim of the agreement was to develop the gas field and to bring gas by pipeline to southern Chittagong.
It said the American Occidental Corp. has also recently agreed to invest $100 million for onshore gas development.
"The projects will increase U.S. investment to more than $200 million, ten times its earlier level," the statement quoted U.S. Ambassador David Merrill as saying.
Merrill said the gas would be used for producing fertiliser and electricity.
